Write a level-of-detail pyramid of A5 cells to Parquet

Source: R/pyramid.R
a5_write_pyramid.Rd

Builds the pyramid of a5_pyramid() and writes it, leaves included, to one Parquet file laid out for a browser to read with HTTP range requests, as with hyparquet. The build and the write run in Rust, so the levels never pass through R.

Usage

a5_write_pyramid(
  x,
  dest,
  ...,
  lods = NULL,
  aggregate = c("mean", "rep_child"),
  reducers = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  types = NULL,
  rep_sd = NULL,
  tile_size = 4096L,
  compression = c("snappy", "zstd", "none"),
  metadata = NULL,
  threads = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A data frame with one a5R::a5_cell column, an a5R::a5_cell vector, or Arrow data with one uint64 column of cells: an Arrow Table, RecordBatch, RecordBatchReader, Dataset or query from the arrow package. The cells must share one resolution and appear once each; rows with NA cells are dropped. An a5R::a5_covering holds cells at mixed resolutions: convert it with a5R::a5_uncompact() first. Arrow data is read into the engine batch by batch without passing through R, so a Dataset over Parquet files (from arrow::open_dataset()) builds without R holding the leaves.

dest

Path of the Parquet file to write. An existing file is replaced. The file is written under a temporary name and renamed when complete, so a failed or interrupted write leaves no partial file.

...

<tidy-select> Value columns to carry into the pyramid. Default: every numeric column other than the cells. For an Arrow Dataset that includes its partitioning columns, such as year from year=2025/ directories, so name the value columns there.

lods

Integer vector of the coarser LODs to build, each below the leaves' resolution; the leaves are always kept. Default: every resolution from 2 up to the leaves'. Resolutions 0 and 1 hold the 12 and 60 largest cells, which no map view draws.

aggregate

The reducer for every value column: "mean" (default) or "rep_child". See "Reducers".

reducers

Named character vector of reducers for single columns, overriding aggregate, such as c(count = "sum", class = "mode").

weights

Name of a numeric column of non-negative leaf weights for "mean", "mode" and "rep_child", such as the npix column from a5px::a5_read_raster(). NA weights count as 0, and leaves with weight 0 do not count. Default NULL: every leaf counts once.

types

Named character vector of storage types for single columns, such as c(red = "uint8", ndvi = "float32"). See "Column types".

rep_sd

Named numeric vector of standard deviations for "rep_child" columns, such as c(red = 60, green = 60). Default NULL: each column's standard deviation over the leaves, or 1 where that is 0 or undefined (a constant column). That depends on every leaf, so pyramids built from different parts of a region choose representatives differently even where their cells are the same; fix the standard deviations (from a whole-region build's a5_pyramid_info()$columns$sd, say) for builds whose cells must agree.

tile_size

The most rows in a tile (row group). Larger tiles mean fewer requests and a smaller footer; smaller tiles mean less data fetched outside the view. Default: 4096.

compression

"snappy" (default), "zstd" or "none". hyparquet decodes snappy itself; zstd needs the hyparquet-compressors package in the browser.

metadata

Named character vector or list of strings to add to the file's key-value metadata, such as a renderer's settings as JSON. The keys "a5pyramid", "a5_index" and "ARROW:schema" are reserved.

threads

Number of threads, or NULL (default) for a5pyramid_threads().

Value

dest, invisibly.

File layout

Each level is split into tiles of at most tile_size rows, and each tile is one Parquet row group. Levels follow each other in ascending LOD order, coarsest first. A tile is a run of consecutive cell ids: A5 ids follow a space-filling curve, so such a run is a compact patch of the globe. A level is split down the A5 index hierarchy only where a run holds more than tile_size cells, which makes tiles coarse where data is sparse and fine where it is dense, and keeps every level sorted by cell id.

The file's key-value metadata holds a JSON index under "a5pyramid": the leaves' resolution, the value columns with their types and reducers, each level's LOD, row count and tiles, and the bounding box of each tile, computed from its cells' boundaries. A reader fetches the footer, picks the level for the zoom and the tiles whose boxes meet the view, and decodes only those row groups. "a5_index" records the A5 index version of the ids, "1.0", as across the a5R stack.

The columns are cell (uint64), lod (uint8), ncell (uint32) and the value columns with their types, NA stored as null. cell and ncell are delta encoded and lod dictionary encoded; Parquet statistics are kept for cell and lod only, so engines such as DuckDB can skip row groups by LOD or cell while the footer stays small. The format is specified in FORMAT.md in the package source (src/rust/a5pyramid/FORMAT.md), with a reading recipe for hyparquet.

See also

a5_pyramid_info() to inspect the file, a5_read_pyramid() to read levels back, a5_pyramid_arrow() for the same tiles in memory.

Examples

library(a5R)
centre <- a5_lonlat_to_cell(-3.19, 55.95, resolution = 10)
cells <- a5_uncompact(a5_spherical_cap(centre, 3000), resolution = 15)
x <- data.frame(cell = cells, value = runif(length(cells)))

path <- tempfile(fileext = ".parquet")
a5_write_pyramid(x, path, types = c(value = "float32"), tile_size = 1000)
a5_pyramid_info(path)
#> ── a5pyramid file file29306eb17f9b.parquet ─────────────────────────────────────
#> Size: 13.2 KB (footer 4.8 KB)
#> A5 index: 1.0
#> Leaves: resolution 15, 1,024 cells
#> LODs: 2-15 (14 levels)
#> Rows: 1,426
#> Tiles: 15 row groups (tile size 1000)
#> Columns: value <float32, mean>
#> Bbox: -3.2194, 55.9355, -3.127, 56.0338
#> Written by: a5pyramid 0.0.0.9000, a5 crate 1.0.0
